findings.F1: The book loses at the exit, not in the signal: of its 690 trades, all short, the 429 that lasted 3.5 days or less lost 2.00 % gross each, while the 145 lasting 3.5 to 6 days gained +0.80 %, the 104 lasting 6 to 15 days +0.82 % and the 11 longer ones +1.52 %. 71 % of trades closed when the forecast fell back to 0, so a short is cut exactly when the coin climbs back over its close of 30 days earlier. That gives an overall mean of -0.93 % gross and -1.03 % net per trade, with 39 % winners.
findings.F2: The fall the signal predicts is larger over 5 to 10 days than over 3. On the non-overlapping grid in folds B, C, the short's total gain per case is +0.32 % over 3 days (350 cases, t 0.47 with one day's cases together), only 1.5 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade. Over 5 days it is +1.62 % (204 cases, 105 days), 7 times the cost, with an unusual move of +2.84 % (t 2.19). Over 10 days the unusual move is +3.36 % (106 cases, t 1.33).
findings.F3: The effect is graded at every horizon. The deepest third of falls gives an unusual short gain of +2.15 % over 3 days against +0.31 % for the shallowest third (t 2.45 and 0.53, unclustered). Over 5 days it is +3.62 % against +2.00 %, and over 7 days the deepest third gives +5.46 % (53 cases, t 1.87).
findings.F4: The short fights the coins' normal rise. Over all bars in these folds a short earns -0.78 % per 3 days, -1.34 % per 5 and -2.65 % per 10 (t about -4). Choppy bars with no signal give a short -0.82 % per 3 days, so a small 3-day unusual move (+1.02 %) leaves almost no total gain. This is why the book's Sharpe trails holding by 0.46 and it earns 0.020 % a day in position against the 0.05 % needed.
findings.F5: The signal is strongest when the coin's last-10-day swing is above its 30-day swing. Signal cases then earn a total short gain of +4.60 % over 5 days (68 cases, unusual t 2.10) and +9.66 % over 10 days (39 cases, total t 2.80, unusual t 3.45). The same rising swing in choppy bars with no signal loses -8.66 % over 5 days and -12.36 % over 10 days for a short, so the condition is not an effect of its own. It fits the theory: a coin's swing quickens while the month's sellers are still unloading.
findings.F6: A falling last week adds to the signal. Over 3 days, signal cases with a 7-day return at or below 0 earn an unusual short gain of +1.27 % (228 cases, t 2.19), against +0.54 % (t 0.89) when the 7-day return is above 0. Choppy bars with a falling week but no signal earn -0.08 % (115 cases, t -0.11), so the falling week alone carries nothing. Over 7 days, the deep cases with a falling week earn +6.33 % unusual (37 cases, t 1.70).
findings.F7: The result leans on one window, and the effect belongs to the choppy market. w16 has 8 cases over 5 days with a +25.9 % unusual gain, and the book's best daily mean, +0.108 %, is in w16, so one window carries it; still, the 5-day signal is positive in 8 of 12 windows and in every year from 2018 to 2021. Outside the choppy profile, a 30-day fall in a falling market gives a 5-day short only -0.16 % total and +0.98 % unusual (421 cases, t 0.73), well below the +2.84 % inside choppy markets.

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the larger a coin's plain 30-day fall below zero (its close under its close of 30 days earlier), the more it falls over the next 7 days, a fall that keeps going on days when the coin has already climbed back over that 30-day-old close.
ideas.consequence: A short taken on a deep month-long fall in a trendless market should be held for about a week, not closed the moment the coin recovers its month-old price.
ideas.name: choppy month fall, week hold

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the larger a coin's plain 30-day fall below zero, the more it falls over the next 10 days, only while its swing over the last 10 days is larger than its swing over the last 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A deep monthly fall in a trendless market whose daily swings are quickening is a stronger reason to stay short for up to two weeks.
ideas.name: choppy month fall, quickening swing

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the larger a coin's plain 30-day fall below zero, the more it falls over the next 7 days, only while its 7-day return is also below zero.
ideas.consequence: In a trendless market, a short on a deep monthly fall is better taken when the last week is still falling, and held for a week.
ideas.name: choppy month fall, falling week
